question: Why do commercial real estate developers procure signage late in the project timeline, even though visible signage affects leasing velocity?
summary: Late signage procurement is the industry norm. Corpus attributes it to construction coordination friction. First-principles derivation identifies the deeper root: pro forma blindspots that sever signage cost from leasing benefit, plus organizational siloing between construction and leasing teams. Corpus never connects signage timing to leasing velocity. The structural fix (modular structure/panel decoupling enabling early install) is also novel to the corpus. Actionable reframe for Brand 9 Signs: position as leasing velocity instrument, not construction subcontractor.
